thread_text:
Sanjay: Heads-up — CA attempted to scale down nodepool `gpu-eu-west-1a` and the drain hung because of a mix of PDBs and a couple of pods in `Terminating` for >3m. Noticed cost bump and backlog.
Alex: Which PDBs are blocking? Can you paste `kubectl get pdb -n ml` from that cluster?
Sanjay: quick excerpt:
```
NAME                     MIN AVAILABLE   MAX UNAVAILABLE   ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS   AGE
model-serving-pdb        1               0                 0                     12d
batch-embed-pdb          1               0                 0                     5d
```
Lina: model-serving has replicas on every GPU node (anti-affinity). CA tries to pick a node with one replica — pdb prevents eviction.
Morgan: There were also two pods stuck `Terminating` because the finalizer was waiting on our internal shutdown hook (grpc drain) — they didn't honor 30s SIGTERM.
Sanjay: Right. CA's `safe-to-evict` checks saw these and aborted drain. But the node remained cordoned for ~4m which reduced available GPU capacity and pushed traffic to dedicated capacity => cost.
Alex: Could we make the shutdown faster by tweaking the finalizer? Or use a `gracePeriodSeconds` annotation for scale-down path?
Lina: Two parallel fixes: 1) teach our shutdown hook to respond to preemption and finish within 30s; 2) add an autoscaler-aware annotation so CA can prefer nodes with `scale-down-safe=true` pods.
Morgan: Also we should revisit the PDBs: `model-serving-pdb` minAvailable=1 is conservative across a single AZ. For nodepool-scale-down we can allow minAvailable=1 per zone or use topologySpread + pdb per-zone. Long term: move to zonal PDBs.
Sanjay: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: have CA respect a new eviction annotation so critical replicas with stateful cleanup can opt-out of scale-down for X minutes. Eg `redwood.io/scale-down-protected: "true"` and a TTL.
Alex: I can prototype an admission hook that flips `redwood.io/scale-down-protected` for pods that are performing checkpointing. Alternatively, we can add a `preDrain` job: when CA plans to drain, orchestrator calls a webhook that returns `ok`/`wait` (with timeout). CA would need that integration.
autoscaler-bot: CA decision log: scale-down candidate node-9 matched priorities. AbortReason=PodDisruptionBudget, BlockingPods=[model-s-1, batch-embed-3], Timestamp=1769803201
Lina: We also should use priority classes more intentionally: give short-lived batch jobs a lower priorityclass and allow preemption. Long-running model-serving should keep high priority but with better rollout (replica spread) so PDBs don't block.
Morgan: Edge case: preemptible GPU nodes (spot) are cheaper but have abrupt termination. CA picks them for scale-down aggressively. We saw churn because our mix of spot vs on-demand in the nodepool wasn't signaled to scheduling policies.
Sanjay: Proposal list:
- Short term (hotfix): set `redwood.io/scale-down-protected` TTL on pods doing long cleanup; CA ignore nodes where protected pods exist.
- Short term: relax `model-serving-pdb` to be zone-aware (split PDBs) and increase readiness probe toleration so rolling doesn't trigger Terminating delays.
- Medium term: admission webhook + CA webhook handshake to allow orchestrated graceful drain with a 2-min window.
- Medium term: change nodepool tags so CA knows which pools are spot vs reserved and prefers spot first for scale-down.
- Long term: update runtime to ensure fast SIGTERM handling and add sidecar to flush KV cache quickly on SIGTERM.
Alex: I'll open a patch for a `scale-down-protected` annotation and a small chart to flip it during model checkpoints. Will also add a CA metric alert when cordoned nodes > 1 for more than 2m in GPU pools.
Morgan: I'll schedule a short oncall runbook update: how to manually force drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` and how to check pdb blockers.
Lina: For rollout we'll test in `staging-eu` first. If we don't see regressions we can roll to prod next week. Also ping infra-sre for quota checks in eu-west region before moving more replicas there.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 — GPU drain blocked by PDBs, assignees: @Sanjay @Alex, severity: P2
Sanjay: Thanks — I'll take ownership. Will post status updates here. :thumbsup:
